facts.quote: that the President issue an order authorizing said tracts of country described in Mr. Colyer’s letter to be regarded as reservations
facts.note: Kappler prints the Nov. 7, 1871 Interior Secretary recommendation (p. 811, naming the Camp Apache tract in the White Mountains selected for the Coyotero and Chilicco Apaches) with the President's Nov. 9 referral directing the Secretary of War to carry out the recommendations (p. 812). Kappler's heading is "White Mountain or San Carlos Reserve"; the Camp Apache tract had earlier been set apart administratively by the War Department (the Sept. 5, 1871 letter on p. 810 says the White Mountain region "has been set apart by the War Department"). No separate order text names the reservation until Dec. 14, 1872.

facts.quote: Respectfully referred to the Secretary of War, who will take such action as may be necessary to carry out the recommendations of the Secretary of the Interior.
facts.note: President Grant's endorsement approving the recommendation printed at 1 Kappler 811 (same instrument as the preceding entry).

facts.land_area: San Carlos division of the White Mountain Indian Reservation, Arizona
facts.quote: withheld from sale and added to the White Mountain Indian Reservation in said Territory, which addition shall hereafter be known as the “San Carlos division of the
facts.note: Original instrument for the San Carlos land; it added the San Carlos division to the White Mountain Reservation (later separately administered as San Carlos). Later orders (1873-77) restored parts to the public domain.

facts.land_area: White Mountain Indian Reservation (enlarged by San Carlos division), Arizona
facts.quote: withheld from sale and added to the White Mountain Indian Reservation in said Territory, which addition shall hereafter be known as the “San Carlos division of the
facts.note: Enlargement; the order recites the "White Mountain Indian Reservation as now established" and sets out its whole boundary.

facts.land_area: Cahuilla Reservation, San Diego County (now Riverside County), California
facts.quote: Cahuila. — Township 7 south, range 2 east ... withdrawn from sale and set apart as reservations for the permanent use and occupancy of the Mission Indians in Lower California
facts.note: The order lists the tract as "Cahuila"; Kappler heading groups all 1875 tracts as Mission Indian reservations. Later orders (1877-1891) enlarged it.

facts.land_area: Capitan Grande Reservation, San Diego County, California
facts.quote: Capitan Grande. — Township 14 south, range 2 east ... withdrawn from sale and set apart as reservations for the permanent use and occupancy of the Mission Indians in Lower California
facts.note: The Barona and Viejas groups derive from this reservation (separate roster entries not recorded here).

facts.land_area: Pala Reservation, San Diego County, California
facts.quote: Pala. — Township 9 south, range 2 west ... withdrawn from sale and set apart as reservations for the permanent use and occupancy of the Mission Indians in Lower California
facts.note: An earlier Jan. 31, 1870 order set apart the "San Pasqual and Pala Valleys" but was revoked Feb. 17, 1871; the 1875 order is the first surviving one. The 1875 tract was reduced later.

facts.land_area: Sycuan Reservation, San Diego County, California
facts.quote: Sycuan. — Township 16 south, range 1 east ... withdrawn from sale and set apart as reservations for the permanent use and occupancy of the Mission Indians in Lower California
facts.note: Section 13 only.

facts.land_area: Inaja and Cosmit Reservation, San Diego County, California
facts.quote: Inaja. — Township 13 south, range 3 east ... withdrawn from sale and set apart as reservations for the permanent use and occupancy of the Mission Indians in Lower California
facts.note: The order also lists "Cosmit" (OCR reads "Gosmit") as a separate tract; the roster nation holds the combined Inaja and Cosmit Reservation.

facts.land_area: Potrero tract including Rincon, San Diego County, California
facts.quote: Portrero. — Including Rincon ... withdrawn from sale and set apart as reservations for the permanent use and occupancy of the Mission Indians in Lower California
facts.note: The tract is headed "Portrero" (Potrero) and "Including Rincon, Gapich, and La Joya"; Rincon is named. "La Joya" is not matched here to La Jolla (see doubtful).

facts.quote: set aside and reserved for the use and occupancy of the Hualpai Indians
facts.note: Date of the order is Jan. 4, 1883 per OSU record; the Kappler OCR prints "January 1883".

facts.quote: withdrawn from sale and settlement, and set apart for the use and occupancy of said Suppai Indians
facts.note: Replaced by the order of Nov. 23, 1880 (same page), which redefined the boundaries; Suppai = Havasupai (Kappler heading "Suppai (Havasupai) Reserve").

facts.quote: withdrawn from settlement and sale, and set apart for the use and occupancy of the Moqui and such other Indians as the Secretary of the Interior may see fit to settle thereon
facts.note: Moqui = Hopi (Kappler heading "Moqui (Hopi) Reserve").

facts.land_area: Papago Indian Reserve (San Xavier del Bac), Arizona
facts.quote: to be known as the Papago Indian Reserve.
facts.note: First reservation set apart for the Papago (Tohono O'odham); the same order says "set apart for the use of the Papago and such other Indians as it may be desirable to place thereon, the following tract of country around San Xavier del Bac" (1 Kappler 805). The much larger main Tohono O'odham reservation was set aside later (see separate entry).

facts.land_area: Gila Bend Reserve (T. 5 S., R. 5 W., Gila and Salt River meridian), Arizona
facts.quote: withdrawn from sale and settlement and set apart for the use and occupancy of the Papago and other Indians now settled there
facts.note: Second Papago tract; separate land base (now the Gila Bend reservation of the Tohono O'odham Nation); original=false because the San Xavier order (1874) came first.

facts.land_area: Salt River lands (Pima and Maricopa Reserve), Arizona
facts.quote: it is hereby ordered that there be withdrawn from sale and settlement and set apart for the use of said Pima and Maricopa Indians, as an addition to the reservation set apart for said Indians by act of Congress
facts.note: Kappler cross-references the Salt River Reserve to this order ("See Pima and Maricopa or Gila River Res., Ex. order June 14 1879", 1 Kappler 808). The order is framed as an addition to the Gila River reservation and replaced an order of Jan. 10, 1879; the tract lies north of the Gila around the Salt River.

facts.land_area: Gila River (Pima and Maricopa) Reservation, Arizona
facts.quote: authorized and required to set apart the tract ... or tracts of land aforesaid as a reservation for the confederated bands of ... Pimas and Maricopas
facts.note: Congress directed the President to set apart the surveyed Gila River tracts as a reservation (not exceeding 100 square miles); Kappler lists the Gila River Reserve as "established by act of February 28, 1859 (11 Stat., 401), and Executive orders" (1 Kappler 804, 805). The act is a mandate to the President; I have not found a separate order recording the original set-aside, so the act is treated as the original instrument. Enlarged by EOs beginning Aug. 31, 1876.

facts.land_area: Colorado River Reservation (Arizona), lands west of a line from Half-Way Bend to Corner Rock
facts.quote: shall be set apart for an Indian reservation for the Indians of said river and its tributaries
facts.note: Kappler: Colorado River Reserve "established by act of March 3, 1865 (13 Stat., 559), and following Executive orders" (1 Kappler 803). Enlarged by Exec. Orders of Nov. 22, 1873, Nov. 16, 1874 and May 15, 1876.

facts.land_area: Yuma Reserve (Arizona side of the Colorado River opposite the Gila mouth)
facts.quote: withdrawn from settlement and sale and set apart as a reservation for the Yuma and such other Indians as the Secretary of the Interior may see fit to settle thereon
facts.note: This Arizona tract was cancelled and replaced by the Exec. Order of Jan. 9, 1884 (1 Kappler 832) setting apart lands in California; the Fort Yuma Reservation as it exists is the Jan. 9, 1884 tract (see next entry). Kappler also notes the act of Aug. 15, 1894 (28 Stat. 332).

facts.quote: In lieu of an Executive order dated July 6, 1883, setting apart certain lands in the Territory of Arizona as a reservation for the Yuma Indians, which order is hereby cancelled
facts.note: Replacement order; tract in California except the Fort Yuma military reservation.

facts.land_area: Duck Valley Reserve, Idaho and Nevada
facts.quote: And the above-named tract of land is hereby set apart as a reservation for the Western Shoshone Indians
facts.note: Order is printed under the Nevada heading "Duck Valley Reserve"; enlarged by Exec. Order of May 4, 1886 (adding lands for the Paddy Cap band of Pi-Utes).

facts.quote: the following-described lands in the southeastern part of Nevada are hereby set apart for the use of the Indians in that locality
facts.note: Cancelled and replaced by the Exec. Order of Feb. 12, 1874 (1 Kappler 867); Kappler also cites act of Mar. 13, 1875 (18 Stat. 445).

facts.instrument: Letter of Comm'r of Indian Affairs, Nov. 29, 1859, 1 Kappler 868
facts.quote: reserving from sale and settlement, for Indian use, a tract of land in the northern portion of the valley of the Truckee River, including Pyramid Lake
facts.note: Administrative reservation requested of the General Land Office ("to respect said reservations upon the plats of survey"); not an executive order, but Kappler prints it as the first act in the reserve's history, and the Exec. Order of Mar. 23, 1874 (next entry) later confirmed the surveyed reservation. Treat as the original set-aside, subject to the caveat that the legal form is a Commissioner's reservation.

facts.quote: the tract of country known and occupied as the Pyramid Lake Indian Reservation in Nevada, as surveyed by Eugene Monroe, in January, 1865
facts.note: Confirms and sets apart by order the surveyed reservation (withdrawn from sale and set apart for the Pah-Ute and other Indians residing thereon).

facts.instrument: Letter of Comm'r of Indian Affairs, Nov. 29, 1859, 1 Kappler 868
facts.quote: a tract in the northeastern part of the valley of W alker’s River, including Walker’s Lake
facts.note: Same 1859 letter reserves a tract including Walker's Lake; the surveyed Walker River reservation was set apart by Exec. Order of Mar. 19, 1874. Quote OCR spacing ("W alker") is preserved from the scan.

facts.quote: the reservation situated on Walker River, Nevada, as surveyed by Eugene Monroe, December, 1864
facts.note: Withdrawn from public sale and set apart for the Pah-Ute Indians residing thereon; first order directly establishing the surveyed reservation.

facts.land_area: Fort Hall Reserve (southern Idaho reservation for the Boise and Bruneau Shoshones and Bannocks)
facts.quote: Let the lands be set apart as reservations for the Indians within named, as recommended by the Acting Secretary of the Interior.
facts.note: The recommendation printed with the order describes the southern reservation as "The Boise and Bruneau bands of Shoshones and Bannock Reservation ... comprehending Fort Hall" (1 Kappler 836). The July 30, 1869 order (1 Kappler 839) designated this tract as the Bannock reservation under the Treaty of July 3, 1868; Kappler: "This reservation is included in the executive order of June 14, 1867" (1 Kappler 838). Fort Hall boundaries later changed by treaty and acts.

facts.land_area: Northern Idaho reservation for the Coeur d'Alenes and other tribes
facts.quote: Let the lands be set apart as reservations for the Indians within named, as recommended by the Acting Secretary of the Interior.
facts.note: The accompanying recommendation sets apart a northern reservation (about 20 miles square) for "the Cœur d'Alenes and other tribes of northern Idaho" (1 Kappler 836); the reservation was not actually established on the ground until the Exec. Order of Nov. 8, 1873 (next entry). Low confidence that the 1867 tract is the same land.

facts.quote: withdrawn from sale and set apart as a reservation for the Cœur d’Alene Indians, in said Territory
facts.note: First order naming a Coeur d'Alene reservation; enlarged by later orders and the act of Mar. 3, 1891 (26 Stat. 1027).

facts.land_area: Fort Berthold Reserve (Arickaree, Gros Ventre and Mandan Reservation), Dakota Territory
facts.quote: Let the lands indicated in the accompanying diagram be set apart as a reservation for the Arickaree, Gros Ventre, and Mandan Indians
facts.note: Kappler's 1880 order (1 Kappler 883) calls it "the Arickaree, Gros Ventre, and Mandan Reservations set aside by Executive order dated April 12, 1870, and known as the Fort Berthold Reservation." The order is undated in Kappler's OCR ("April 1870") but refers to the Interior letter of the 12th. The Fort Laramie treaty of Sept. 17, 1851 had described a larger territory for these tribes but Kappler lists it as unratified/amended.

facts.quote: withdrawn from sale and settlement and set apart for the use and occupancy of the Turtle Mountain band of Chippewas
facts.note: Restored in large part to the public domain by the Exec. Order of Mar. 29, 1884 (townships 162-163 N. excepted), and amended June 3, 1884 (1 Kappler 885); the later treaty/agreement of 1892 and acts affect the reservation.

facts.instrument: Treaty with the Yakama, June 9, 1855, art. II, 12 Stat. 951, 952
facts.quote: There is, however, reserved, from the lands above ceded ... for the use and occupation of the aforesaid confederated tribes and bands of Indians, the tract of land included within the following boundaries
facts.note: Ratified Mar. 8, 1859; proclaimed Apr. 18, 1859. Kappler also lists the Yakima reserve as established by this treaty and by later orders.

facts.instrument: Treaty with the Nez Perces, June 11, 1855, art. II, 12 Stat. 957
facts.quote: There is, however, reserved from the lands above ceded ... for the use and occupation of the said tribe, and as a general reservation
facts.note: Reduced by the treaty of June 9, 1863, 14 Stat. 647 (the 1863 article again sets apart a reservation in the Clearwater country) and later acts.

facts.instrument: Treaty with the Walla-Wallas, Cayuses, and Umatilla, June 9, 1855, art. I, 12 Stat. 945, 946
facts.quote: shall be set apart as a residence for said Indians
facts.note: Article I cedes the country and sets apart the described tract "shall be held and regarded as an Indian reservation" beginning on the Umatilla River.

facts.land_area: Warm Springs Reservation (tract beginning at the De Chutes River), Oregon
facts.instrument: Treaty with the Tribes of Middle Oregon, June 25, 1855, art. I, 12 Stat. 963, 964
facts.quote: shall, until otherwise directed by the President of the United States, be set apart as a residence for said Indians
facts.note: Boundaries described beginning "in the middle of the channel of the De Chutes River opposite the eastern termination of a range of high lands usually known as the Mutton Mountains."

facts.instrument: Treaty of Hell Gate, July 16, 1855, art. II, 12 Stat. 975
facts.quote: There is, however, reserved from the lands above ceded, ... for the use and occupation of the said confederated tribes, and as a general Indian reservation
facts.note: Kappler lists the Jocko Reserve (Flathead Agency) as "established by treaty July 16, 1855" (1 Kappler 859).

facts.instrument: Treaty with the Makah, Jan. 31, 1855, art. II, 12 Stat. 939
facts.quote: the following tract of land, viz.: Commencing on ... the beach at the mouth of a small brook running into Neah Bay
facts.note: Enlarged by Exec. Orders of Oct. 26, 1872 (replaced Jan. 2, 1873) and Oct. 21, 1873.

facts.instrument: Treaty of Medicine Creek, Dec. 26, 1854, art. II, 10 Stat. 1132
facts.quote: The small island called Klah-che-min, situated opposite the mouths of Hammersley’s and Totten’s inlets
facts.note: Art. II: "There is, however, reserved for the present use and occupation of the said tribes and bands, the following tracts of land."

facts.land_area: Nisqually tract near the mouth of She-nah-nam Creek, Washington
facts.instrument: Treaty of Medicine Creek, Dec. 26, 1854, art. II, 10 Stat. 1132
facts.quote: a square tract containing two sections, or twelve hundred and eighty acres, on Puget’s Sound, near the mouth of the She-nah-nam Creek
facts.note: Treaty tract identified with the Nisqually reservation by location (She-nah-nam = Sequalitchew/Nisqually); the later Exec. Order of Jan. 20, 1857 enlarged it (not read).

facts.quote: named in communication of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs dated the 8th instant, and for such other Indians as the Department of the Interior may see fit to locate thereon

facts.quote: be, and the same is hereby, set apart as a reservation for said Indians, and for such other Indians as the Department of the Interior may see fit to locate thereon
facts.note: The order restores the Apr. 9 tract to the public domain and, "in lieu thereof," sets apart the country bounded east and south by the Columbia River, west by the Okanogan River and north by the British possessions. facts.quote: withdrawn from sale and settlement and set apart for the permanent use and occupation of the Quillehute Indians

facts.quote: set aside and reserved for the use and occupancy of the Spokane Indians

facts.note: Congress confirmed the Pueblo's land claim (Spanish-era grant) as reported by the New Mexico surveyor general and directed the Commissioner of the General Land Office to survey and issue a patent. facts.note: Order does not itself name the Shoalwater; Kappler's heading "Shoalwater Reserve" (and OSU) identify it, and Kappler records it as occupied by Shoalwater and Chehalis. Date Sept. 22, 1866 per OSU; Kappler prints "September 1866".

facts.instrument: Proclamation of Austin Wiley, Superintendent of Indian Affairs for California, Aug. 21, 1864 (under Act of Apr. 8, 1864, 13 Stat. 39), 1 Kappler 815
facts.quote: I have this day located an Indian reservation ... Settlers in Hoopa Valley are hereby notified
facts.note: Located by the California Superintendent under the Act of Apr. 8, 1864, 13 Stat. 39 (which authorized up to four reservations), "subject to the approval of the President." The day is legible in the earlier Kappler print (Fort Gaston, Aug. 21, 1864); the 1904 print's OCR gives "August 1861" (the year is 1864). Boundaries were fixed by Exec. Order of June 23, 1876. Page 815 per the running page number.

facts.land_area: Hoopa Valley Indian Reservation, California (89,572.43 acres)
facts.quote: declared to be the exterior boundaries of Hoopa Valley Indian Reservation
facts.note: Confirms the Hoopa Valley Reservation as one of the reservations authorized by the Act of Apr. 8, 1864 (13 Stat. 39) and fixes its boundaries. Extended along the Klamath River by Exec. Order of Oct. 16, 1891.

facts.instrument: Order of the Secretary of the Interior (Nov. 18, 1858), as recited in Commissioner's letter of Jan. 6, 1860, 1 Kappler 824-825
facts.quote: the entire valley of Nome Cult, designated by you as the Round Valley, was set apart and reserved for Indian purposes
facts.note: The Nov. 18, 1858 Commissioner's letter to Superintendent Henley (1 Kappler 824-825) conveys the Secretary's direction that "the entire Nome Cult Valley shall be retained as a reservation." The 1860 letter cited is the source read for the quotation. Later made one of the Act of Apr. 8, 1864 (13 Stat. 39) reservations; boundaries fixed by Exec. Orders (1870 onward). Not an executive order or statute in the first instance; confidence low.

facts.quote: Let the lands described in the within letter be set apart as a reservation for the bands of Indians in California therein named
facts.note: Canceled and replaced "in lieu" by the Exec. Order of Oct. 3, 1873 for the same bands.

facts.quote: set apart as a reservation for the Tule River, King’s River, Owen’s River, Manche Cajon, and other scattered bands of Indians in the State of California
facts.note: Replaces the Jan. 9, 1873 tract; later enlarged by Exec. Orders (1878, 1886).

facts.instrument: Executive indorsement of President Buchanan, June 30, 1857, 1 Kappler 886
facts.quote: withdrawn from sale and entry and set apart as a reservation for Indian purposes till otherwise ordered
facts.note: The 1904 print's OCR gives the year as 1867; the earlier print and the signer (James Buchanan) show 1857. The order does not itself name Grande Ronde; Kappler's heading "Grande Ronde Reserve" and the Secretary's letter ("Willamette tribes, parties to treaty of January, 1855") identify it. Grand Ronde descends from the Treaties of Jan. 22, 1855 (Molala etc.) and Dec. 21, 1855.

facts.quote: The reservation of the land within denoted by blue-shaded lines is hereby made
facts.note: Kappler gives the order under "Siletz (originally known as Coast) Reserve." Conditional reservation for the Coast tribes; curtailed by Exec. Order of Dec. 1866 and Act of Mar. 3, 1875 (18 Stat. 446). The Siletz Reservation was terminated in 1956 and restored in 1977; the current Census area is trust land.

facts.quote: set apart as a reservation for the use and occupation of the Northern Cheyenne Indians
facts.note: Kappler: "established by Executive orders only." Enlarged and redefined by Exec. Order of Mar. 19, 1900 (1 Kappler 860-861) and later orders.

facts.land_area: Reservation of six sections at the head of Hood's Canal, Washington
facts.instrument: Treaty of Point No Point, Jan. 26, 1855, art. II, 12 Stat. 934 (art. II begins at 933)
facts.quote: amount of six sections, or three thousand eight hundred and forty acres, situated at the head of Hood’s Canal, to be hereafter set apart
facts.note: The preamble names the S'Klallam villages and the Sko-ko-mish, Too-an-hooch and Chem-a-kum tribes. The tract was 'to be hereafter set apart' and was fixed later by Exec. Order of Feb. 25, 1874.

facts.quote: withdrawn from sale or other disposition and set apart for the use of the S’Klallam Indians the following tract of country on Hood’s Canal
facts.note: Describes the tract beginning at the mouth of the Skokomish River, inclusive of the six treaty sections.

facts.instrument: Treaty of Fort Bridger, July 3, 1868, art. II, 15 Stat. 673, 674
facts.quote: shall be and the same is set apart for the absolute and undisturbed use and occupation of the Shoshonee Indians herein named
facts.note: Boundaries run from the mouth of Owl Creek along the Wind River Mountains. The Northern Arapaho are not party to this treaty (see doubtful list).

facts.instrument: Treaty with the Omahas, Mar. 16, 1854, art. 1, 10 Stat. 1043, 1044
facts.quote: which is reserved by the ... for their future home
facts.note: Reserve described as the country "north of said due west line".

facts.land_area: Winnebago Reservation, Nebraska (land ceded by the Omaha, Mar. 6, 1865)
facts.instrument: Treaty with the Winnebago, Mar. 8, 1865, art. II, 14 Stat. 671, 672
facts.quote: the United States agree to set apart for the ... occupation and future home of the Winnebago Indians, forever
facts.note: Land taken from the Omaha cession of Mar. 6, 1865.

facts.instrument: Treaty with the Yankton Sioux, Apr. 19, 1858, art. I, 11 Stat. 743, 744
facts.quote: except four hundred ... thousand acres thereof, situated and described as follows
facts.note: Reserved tract on the Missouri River, mouth of the Choteau (Chouteau) Creek north.

facts.instrument: Treaty with the Sisseton and Wahpeton, Feb. 19, 1867, art. III, 15 Stat. 505, 506
facts.quote: shall be set apart for the members of said bands who have heretofore surrendered to the authorities of the government ... the following described lands as a perma nent reservation
facts.note: Art. IV set apart a separate reservation (Devils Lake, now Spirit Lake) for other members and the Cuthead Yanktonai; that is not the roster nation here.

facts.instrument: Treaty with the Chippewa of the Mississippi, Mar. 19, 1867, art. II, 16 Stat. 719, 720
facts.quote: there is hereby set apart for their use a tract of land, to be located in a square form as nearly as possible ... which reservation shall include White Earth Lake and Rice Lake, and contain thirty-six townships of land
facts.note: Treaty also reserves a tract for the Mississippi bands (Gull Lake / Mille Lacs, Leech Lake) in art. I.

facts.instrument: Treaty with the Bois Forte Band, Apr. 7, 1866, art. III, 1st, 14 Stat. 765-766
facts.quote: for the perpetual use and occupancy of said Bois Forte band of Chippewas, a tract of land of not less than one hundred thousand acres
facts.note: The treaty directed selection of a tract including Nett Lake; The treaty only authorized selection of the tract; the later instruments that fixed the Nett Lake and Deer Creek lands were not located here. Recorded as the first authorization.

facts.instrument: Agreement of Dec. 28, 1886, ratified by Act of May 1, 1888, ch. 213, 25 Stat. 113
facts.quote: the separate reservation for the Indians now attached to and receiving rations at the, Fort Peck Agency, Montana, shall be bounded as follows
facts.note: Agreement (Dec. 28, 1886) ratified by Congress; it carves the separate Fort Peck reservation out of the larger Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfeet and River Crow reservation created by Exec. Order of July 5, 1873 (1 Kappler 855-856), which does not name the Assiniboine or Sioux. The act names "Indians now attached to ... Fort Peck Agency," not the Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes by name.

facts.instrument: Agreement of Jan. 21, 1887, ratified by Act of May 1, 1888, ch. 213, 25 Stat. 113
facts.quote: the separate reservation for the Indians now attached to and receiving rations at the Fort Belknap Agency shall be bounded as follows
facts.note: Carved out of the reservation of Exec. Order of July 5, 1873 (1 Kappler 855-856). The act names "Indians now attached to ... Fort Belknap Agency," not the Gros Ventre and Assiniboine by name.

facts.land_area: Rocky Boy's Reservation (about 56,035 acres of the former Fort Assinniboine Military Reservation), Montana
facts.quote: apart as a reservation for Rocky Boy’s Band of Chippewas and such other homeless Indians in the State of Montana
facts.note: An earlier appropriation act authorized the Secretary to settle Rocky Boy's Band on public land or purchase land; it did not itself set land aside.
